title: Procurement intake: technical acceptance criteria + escalation path - Crestwood
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + latest DPA redline by 2026-11-12
SE to run 48h POC performance run and share results by 2026-11-18
Pricing team to provide committed tier quote by 2026-11-13
Customer to confirm internal approvals path and stakeholder list by 2026-11-15
action_items: Priya - provision isolated POC env and run perf tests - due 2026-11-18
Alex - send redlined DPA and MSA summary + SOC2 link - due 2026-11-12
Mark - circulate procurement approval matrix and expected PO cadence - due 2026-11-15
Dana - provide list of required encryption/KMS controls and acceptance criteria - due 2026-11-16
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jonas Reed (Redwood CSM), Mark Elias (Crestwood Procurement), Dana Ross (Crestwood CISO), Elena Varela (Crestwood Counsel), Samir Patel (Crestwood Cloud)

Summary (auto): Procurement and security intake to confirm acceptance criteria for pilot/proof-of-concept, discuss MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing pathway and escalation process for Dedicated vs Hosted and potential private VPC deployment.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can we do quick intros? I'll kick it off. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE covering Crestwood.
[00:12] Mark: Hi, Mark here, procurement lead. We handle vendor intake and approvals.
[00:16] Dana: Dana, CISO. I'll focus on security and ops acceptance.
[00:20] Elena: Elena, legal counsel, I'm here for contract redlines.
[00:23] Samir: Samir, cloud architect, I'll validate network/KMS constraints.
[00:28] Priya (SE): Priya, Redwood SE, I'll own the technical POC and perf runs.
[00:33] Jonas (CSM): Jonas, post-sales CSM, covering onboarding expectations.

[01:05] Alex: Cool. Objective today: make sure we align on what counts as a successful pilot, what contract items we need to close, and where pricing approvals sit. We'll also talk escalation processes if we hit SLO/SLA issues.

[02:12] Mark: Quick context — procurement needs: MSA + DPA must be in place for any pilot above 30k monthly, and we need the commercial terms up front. The finance folks want an outline of PO cadence. Also, security review needs the SOC2 report and KMS architecture details.

[02:45] Dana: Yes, and to add, we have a hard requirement for customer-managed keys (KMS) in a BYOK pattern for any PII inference. We also expect audit logs exported to our SIEM and retention controls.

[03:10] Priya: Understood. For the POC we can spin a dedicated allocation in Redwood Dedicated or run a private VPC deployment. For BYOK we have an integration path w/ major KMS providers; the integration might add a week or two. But we should scope the acceptance tests so we don't block the initial perf runs.

[04:05] Samir: Two clarifying Qs — 1) If we go with hosted dedicated, where do the keys live? 2) How do we validate that no cleartext model artifacts leave the node?

[04:28] Priya: Good questions. Hosted Dedicated means Redwood manages GPUs but we support envelope encryption: customer keys can be stored in HSM/KMS and we do envelope encrypt for checkpoints at rest. For private deployment (VPC) you run the control plane in your VPC and keys remain under your KMS. Regarding model artifacts, our runtime writes checkpoints to encrypted volumes; we have an attestable workflow and can share a tech note. I'll link the runbook.

[05:12] Elena: On DPA/MSA redlines: our legal team will need to see data retention, deletion mechanics, subprocessors, and breach notification timelines. We have standard language for subprocessor lists and will request a 30-day notification for additions. What's Redwood's default there?

[05:34] Alex: Default is we provide a subprocessor list and 30 days notice for major changes; smaller infra provider swaps are within our ops carve-outs but we can surface them. For breach notifications we do our standard 72-hour notification to customers after we confirm impact.

[06:01] Elena: We typically push for 48-hour notice, but we can be pragmatic on proof of impact timing. We'll flag any deviation in the redline.

[06:20] Mark: Pricing — for the pilot we need committed tier pricing to evaluate budget. Is there a short-term pilot tier or do we need to convert to a month-to-month committed seat? Finance wants the landed monthly estimate including ingress/egress and storage costs.

[06:44] Alex: We can propose a time-limited pilot rate (committed compute for 4 weeks) and give a provisional committed tier quote. I'll loop in pricing and send a spreadsheet. We'll include token estimate, storage, and egress.

[07:12] Dana: SLA question — our app is latency-sensitive. We need to understand Redwood's SLOs for tail latency and scheduled maintenance windows. Also, what's the escalation path if latency consistently breaches our SLO?

[07:33] Priya: For Hosted API we have published p50/p95/p99 latency benchmarks per model. For Dedicated we can commit to tighter latency SLAs in the Dedicated contract (custom). Typically escalation goes AE -> SE -> Infra ops -> SRE bridge; we can map a 24/7 escalation path for enterprise customers, and include on-call contact for production incidents.

[08:05] Jonas: And for the POC we often do an initial 48h continuous load test to characterize tail behavior; if that looks good we proceed to the next step.

[08:35] Samir: On network — can Redwood peer with our VPC? We require private connectivity with restricted egress, ideally VPC peering or Direct Connect equivalent.

[08:52] Priya: Yes, for Private deployment we support VPC peering and private link options. For Hosted Dedicated we can set up private link into a customer VPC for data path. Both are possible; peering will have different networking considerations.

[09:20] Mark: Wanted to raise one red flag from procurement side: our purchasing policy wants to see indemnity and cap language in the MSA; we may have a exceptions request. How flexible is Redwood around caps?

[09:38] Alex: We typically have standard liability caps tied to fees paid in prior 12 months; for enterprise customers we can negotiate. We'll need legal to exchange redlines.

[09:55] Elena: We'll prepare a redline and highlight the clauses. Expect questions on data residency and encryption at rest.

[10:08] Dana: Operational acceptance criteria — concretely: 1) proof that audit logs are forwarded to our Splunk or SIEM, 2) BYOK validated, 3) latency within agreed p95 threshold under our baseline load, 4) evidence of role-based access controls and admin RBAC, 5) can we get a runbook for failover?

[10:40] Priya: We can deliver that. For audit logs we can stream to S3 or push to syslog/Splunk; Samir, which does Crestwood prefer?

[10:50] Samir: Prefer direct syslog or Splunk HTTP event collector. S3 is okay as fallback but they'd rather we avoid stitching.

[11:02] Priya: Noted. We'll confirm Splunk HEC setup options in the POC doc.

[11:18] Alex: Let's talk timeline. If legal shares a redline by Friday 11/12, and we provision the POC the following Monday, can we expect perf results by the 18th? Priya, feasible?

[11:31] Priya: Yes, assuming keys and network are provisioned. The BYOK step may add a week but we can run a non-BYOK perf run to validate latency and then lock BYOK later. That gives initial results.

[12:00] Mark: For procurement to approve, we need pricing and a pilot statement of work — minimal scope and acceptance criteria. Can you provide a one-page SOW?

[12:12] Jonas: Jonas here — we have a template SOW for pilots that we can adapt. We'll send a one-page SOW with success criteria and target metrics.

[12:25] Elena: On DPA specifics: Are subprocessors published? We need the list of infra partners and where data crosses regions. Crestwood requires EU data residency for certain customers — how does Redwood handle regional residency?

[12:45] Alex: We support region pinning for hosting. For Hosted API some models are available in particular regions; we can match region and ensure logs and storage are kept in-region for EU. Subprocessors list is published, we'll send current roster.

[13:10] Samir: One more architecture ask — do you cache KV across requests? We have concerns about persisted KV data that might include customer context. Is KV segmented per tenant?

[13:27] Priya: Yes, KV cache is per-tenant and sharded; we can flush prefixes on request and we don't use shared caches across tenants. We'll include details in the technical appendix.

[13:50] Mark: Ok great. Let's move into escalation path specifics — if performance breaches SLO for 48h, what's the contractual remedy? Does Redwood offer service credits?

[14:03] Alex: For Dedicated contracts we include credits or SLA remediation clauses; for pilots it's typically operational expenses only but we can discuss making the pilot count toward committed term if thresholds are hit. We'll have pricing/legal propose the options.

[14:30] Dana: For security incidents we want a clear path: notify customer within X hours, provide mitigation plan, and provide audit trail. Also, who is our point of contact? We need a named security liaison.

[14:50] Jonas: We'll nominate a security contact and include an escalation matrix in the SOW.

[15:05] Elena: Small note — Crestwood legal will likely ask for a change control clause on subprocessors and a right to audit for high-risk data processing. How does Redwood handle audit requests?

[15:22] Alex: We offer SOC2 reports and reasonable audit rights; for on-prem/private deployments customers have broader audit capability. For Hosted we can accommodate third-party assessments under NDA; we do limit internal ops visibility.

[15:45] Samir: Network ACLs — we want to control egress to only our endpoints. Can you lock outbound traffic at the node level?

[15:58] Priya: Yes, in private VPC you control egress. In hosted models we can restrict by IP allowlist and private link. We'll document the options.

[16:20] Mark: Let's cover pricing approval path: who signs off at Redwood on special pilot discounts? I need a contact to speed the PO process.

[16:32] Alex: I will own the commercial approval up to X; beyond that I'll escalate to our pricing team. I'll cc the pricing lead when I send the spreadsheet.

[16:45] Elena: For the MSA redline, expect us to request data deletion on termination, clear exit assistance, and SSP fingerprints for subprocessors.

[16:55] Alex: Agreed. We'll provide an exit playbook.

[17:10] Priya: On technical acceptance tests — propose we run: 1) 48h continuous token throughput run with synthetic KVs, 2) BYOK validation (where we rotate keys), 3) Splunk log ingestion test, 4) latency p95 under 200ms for model X (we should pick exact model). Any objections?

[17:36] Dana: p95 <200ms is tight depending on model choice; what's model X? If it's a larger open model we may not hit that. Samir, we should agree on the model class.

[17:50] Samir: Let's start with a small-ish model equivalent to 7B class for baseline; depending on quality we can move to 13B.

[18:02] Priya: Great — we'll recommend the 7B equivalent for latency baseline. Also worth noting quantization and batching choices will affect cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll include those knobs.

[18:25] Mark: Another procurement Q — insurance requirements. Crestwood requires a general liability and cyber policy. Do you have certificates?

[18:36] Alex: Yes, we can provide certs and insurer details. We'll attach them to the procurement packet.

[18:45] Elena: On data residency again — any cross-border subprocessors will need explicit mention. We will flag if any EU data flows to US.

[19:00] Alex: We'll provide a data flow map and subprocessors list.

[19:12] Jonas: I'll follow up on onboarding timelines and provide the SOW template within 24 hours.

[19:25] Mark: Great. Can we get a single doc that bundles: SOW, pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 link, subprocessors list, POC runbook, and the MSA/DPA redline? Procurement prefers a single packet to route internally.

[19:40] Alex: Yes, we'll bundle and send.

[20:00] Priya: Quick technical caveat — if you need BYOK for the initial run it will delay the perf results. We recommend running the perf baseline without BYOK first, then validate BYOK integration. That shortens initial timeline.

[20:20] Dana: That works as long as we get the key rotation and BYOK validation before any live data touches the system.

[20:32] Samir: We'll stand up a test VPC and provide firewall rules and a Splunk endpoint for logging.

[20:40] Alex: Okay, let's role this into a timeline. Actions: Legal redline by 11/12; Redwood sends packet by 11/12; POC provisioned week of 11/15; perf results by 11/18; pricing committed tier quote by 11/13.

[21:05] Elena: One question about the DPA — does Redwood offer data subject request support and a mechanism to search and delete user records across tokenized logs?

[21:20] Priya: We do have tooling for targeted deletion across stored logs and user metadata; token stream retention varies by product, we'll detail exact retention windows.

[21:45] Mark: Ok that should cover procurement needs. A couple of downstream items: 1) Can Redwood supply an internal technical contact for our security review? 2) Will there be an operations onboarding checklist?

[22:02] Jonas: I'll be the ops onboarding contact and will provide the checklist and Runbook.

[22:15] Priya: I'll be the technical contact for the POC.

[22:22] Dana: Good. For escalation, we want named contacts and phone numbers attached to the SOW.

[22:30] Alex: We'll include an on-call rotation and a primary escalation contact.

[22:45] Elena: About the subcontractors — for any 3rd party storage or logging we want to pre-approve high risk providers.

[22:58] Alex: Understood. We'll flag that in the packet.

[23:12] Mark: Anything from the Redwood side on procurement?

[23:20] Alex: Just that we'll try to keep contractual exceptions minimal to shorten cycles; we can take a few key asks for negotiation.

[23:35] Priya: I'll follow up with the technical appendix and will request test accounts from Samir.

[23:48] Samir: I'll send firewall and Splunk endpoints by tomorrow.

[24:00] Jonas: On training — after POC acceptance we'll do a 2-hr enablement workshop with dev and infra teams.

[24:12] Mark: Noted.

[24:20] Elena: Quick legal question — do you have a standard export control clause? We need to vet for our international customers.

[24:35] Alex: Yes we have an export compliance section in the MSA; we'll highlight it.

[24:48] Dana: If we encounter a bug that affects model outputs and causes a security exposure, how quickly can Redwood roll a hotfix?

[24:58] Priya: We push high-severity fixes ASAP; for infra-level issues we can run a hotpatch within hours; we'll define severities and expected windows in the SOW.

[25:20] Mark: Any requirement from procurement for a PO threshold to start the pilot? We typically prefer a minimal PO to cover initial costs.

[25:32] Alex: We can accept a small PO or work on a trial-credit basis and then issue a PO prior to any committed term. We'll outline those options in the packet.

[25:45] Elena: Regarding the DPA, we may request a data processor Addendum that includes specifics on subprocessors and deletion timelines.

[25:58] Alex: We'll provide a standard DPA and be open to narrow edits.

[26:15] Priya: Technical note: for the load run we'll instrument tracing so we can show latency heatmaps and tail distributions.

[26:28] Samir: Perfect. That will help our SRE folks.

[26:40] Alex: Anything else critical we haven't covered?

[26:48] Mark: One small ask — can Redwood include a table of expected monthly cost ranges for 10k/50k/200k tokens per day? Procurement needs a ballpark.

[26:58] Alex: We'll include a token-based cost table and an example invoice.

[27:10] Elena: Does Redwood support SAML SSO for the console? We'll need SSO + SCIM for user provisioning.

[27:22] Priya: Yes, SAML and SCIM are supported. We'll include the SSO metadata file in the packet.

[27:35] Dana: Are there role separation controls so that devs don't have access to customer KMS?

[27:44] Priya: Yes RBAC can be scoped so that only named admins have KMS access and we audit admin actions.

[28:00] Mark: Okay, let's confirm deliverables and owners one more time.

[28:10] Alex: Deliverables: 1) Packet (SOW, pricing sheet, SOC2 link, subprocessors list, POC runbook, MSA/DPA draft) — owner Alex — due 2026-11-12. 2) POC environment and perf run — owner Priya — due 2026-11-18. 3) Procurement approval matrix — owner Mark — due 2026-11-15. 4) Security key list and BYOK criteria — owner Dana/Samir — due 2026-11-16.

[28:45] Mark: Sounds good. We'll expect the packet and then route the PO after finance review.

[29:00] Jonas: I'll also create the onboarding checklist and schedule the enablement workshop for week after POC acceptance.

[29:10] Elena: One last thing — please include the exception request template in the packet so procurement can prefill any cap or indemnity asks.

[29:22] Alex: Will do.

[29:30] Priya: I'll follow up in email with the perf plan and the Splunk ingestion checklist.

[29:40] Samir: I'll provide firewall rules and HEC endpoint by tomorrow EOD.

[29:48] Mark: Thanks everyone. If legal gets the redline by Friday we'll try to keep this moving.

[29:56] Alex: Thanks — we'll send the packet and the DPA redline summary.

[30:05] [cross-talk / brief pause] [laughter]

[30:25] Alex: Recap: packet by 11/12, POC week of 11/15, perf results by 11/18, named contacts in SOW. Any objections?

[30:38] Dana: No objections.

[30:42] Elena: No objections, we'll send redline.

[30:46] Mark: Okay.

[30:50] Alex: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the POC kickoff and the enablement session.

[31:05] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[31:07] Jonas: Bye.
[31:10] Samir: Bye.

Notes and references mentioned: Pricing spreadsheet (will be attached in packet), SOC2 report link: https://redwood.example.com/soc2-2026 (placeholder), DPA template link: https://redwood.example.com/dpa (placeholder), POC runbook: internal link to be sent.
